facts.buildMode: CPython interpreter resolved by `uv sync --locked` from the committed uv.lock; compiled pydantic-core and pyarrow extensions; assertions off; the Pi Durable storage worker is a fresh Node helper process per service open; no debug or instrumented builds anywhere in the loop
facts.declaredMachine: The Linux runner the measurements below ran on. SPEC.md section 19 names a declared Linux machine with 16 GiB memory; this runner exposes the memory recorded here, which is below that class, so the comparison against the targets carries that deviation openly.

reproduce: uv run --locked python3 scripts/benchmark_round1.py (the pinned environment comes from `uv sync --locked`)

results.measurement: runtime.compiler.compile_document over the JSON document bytes with catalogs parsed once (cached catalogs)
results.name: compile-32-projection
results.notes: The sample covers the seven stages from decoding to the built plan; the catalogs stay parsed across samples, which is the cached condition of the target.

target.metric: Compile a 32-projection document with cached catalogs

results.condition: cold: fresh process per sample, kernel page cache warm
results.measurement: one compile in a fresh interpreter: process start, imports, catalog parsing, and one compile_document call
results.name: compile-32-projection-cold-process
results.notes: Context for the warm target above: a cold process pays interpreter and import costs no in-process compile sees. No section 19 target governs this condition.

results.condition: warm: one owning service session, fsynced commits
results.measurement: framed workspace.apply of one bound parameter.set (the service side of a control edit)
results.name: control-feedback-commit
results.notes: Round 1 measures the service side: the framed round trip that validates, compiles the candidate, reserves the generation of the bound action, replaces its pending intent, and commits durably. Native feedback latency is a round 2 measurement. Model and Python execution are absent from the sample.

results.condition: warm: one owning service session, fsynced commits
results.measurement: framed workspace.apply of one entity.replace (projection title) with its candidate compilation
results.name: committed-patch
results.notes: The commit alone. No section 19 target governs the commit without its notification.

results.condition: warm: one owning service session, fsynced commits
results.measurement: the same committed patch plus the workspace.subscribe answer a host applies to make the change visible
results.name: committed-patch-notification
results.notes: Round 1 measures the service side of the committed-patch target: apply round trip plus the ordered notification that carries the change to the visible interface. Python and model time are absent by construction.

target.metric: Small committed patch to visible update

results.condition: warm: fsynced artifact and commit paths in the owning session
results.measurement: WorkspaceService.publish_run of one succeeded run: staged-output verification, immutable artifact finalization with file and directory synchronization, eligibility recheck, source version allocation, and the receipted commit
results.name: artifact-publication
results.notes: Each sample publishes a fresh run of the section 13.2 script shape; 2161 bytes of staged Parquet output. The runner process time is excluded: the target of section 19 is the publication machinery, not Python execution.

results.condition: warm: decoded table cached in the owning service

results.condition: warm: kernel page cache; empty service cache
results.measurement: unsorted first page with empty service cache
results.name: table-page-cache-miss
results.notes: Includes decoding and combining Arrow chunks for later pages.

results.condition: warm: artifact bytes in the kernel page cache
results.measurement: framed table.page at offset 0, limit 50, sorted by the score column descending over every row
